principles.name: Async by default for non-critical paths
principles.statement: Use asynchronous messaging for any integration not on the critical synchronous path
principles.rationale: Async messaging decouples failure domains and absorbs throughput variability
implications: New integrations default to event-driven; sync calls require justification
Producers publish events to a broker rather than calling consumers directly
Consumers must be idempotent — duplicates are normal

principles.name: Contracts before code
principles.statement: API and event schemas are authored, reviewed, and published before implementation begins
principles.rationale: Implementation-driven contracts leak internal models and lock in design errors
implications: OpenAPI / AsyncAPI specs are the source of truth for any integration
Mocked services produced from the spec are available before the producer is built
Breaking changes to a published contract follow a documented deprecation lifecycle

principles.name: Versioned interfaces with explicit deprecation
principles.statement: Every published interface carries a semantic version; obsolete versions remain available for a documented period before retirement
principles.rationale: Silent breaking changes erode trust; permanent backward-compatibility ossifies the estate
implications: Major version bumps require explicit consumer migration plans
Deprecated versions emit telemetry that surfaces remaining consumers

principles.name: Mediated through the gateway
principles.statement: All inter-system traffic crossing a trust boundary passes through the managed API gateway or messaging broker
principles.rationale: Centralised mediation is the only practical control point for auth, rate limiting, observability, and audit
implications: Direct service-to-service URLs across zones are network-policy denied
CI checks flag hard-coded inter-zone endpoints
Gateway and broker capacity scales as a strategic platform, not per-consumer

principles.name: Idempotency is the consumer's contract
principles.statement: Event consumers handle duplicate delivery gracefully; producers do not guarantee exactly-once
principles.rationale: Exactly-once across distributed systems is hard and expensive; idempotency is cheaper and more robust
implications: Consumers maintain deduplication state where required
Producers may retry without coordinating with consumers

principles.name: Internal model does not leak into the integration model
principles.statement: Published events and API payloads express domain concepts in shared language, not the producer's internal data structures
principles.rationale: Leaked internal models tightly couple consumers to producer implementation choices
implications: Producer-internal IDs and structures are translated at the boundary
Shared concepts (per DAT-DAC) are used in payloads where they exist
Internal schema changes do not propagate without explicit contract review
